Prokhorov, the cloakroom attendant.
437:
But we couldn't check it.
Prokhorov didn't show up for their meeting.
438:
He probably suspected something.
He quit his job and hasn't gone home.
440:
We owe you a thousand apologies
and enormous thanks. Take off the wig,
wash off the tattoos,
441:
go home and celebrate New Year.
Thank you very much.
- What about my men?
442: We'll return your charges to prison today.
443:
If you find the cloakroom attendant,
might you need us again?
444:
I didn't want to tell you,
but Bely—the real Docent—escaped today.
445:
Unbelievable, but true.
It's dangerous for you to keep up this disguise.
446:
Could it wait until tomorrow?
It's New Year, and they did try, in their own way.
447:
We're outside the city.
It's very unlikely Docent could find us.
448:
All right, but don't leave the house!
We forwarded your letter
449:
to Sheremetyev's wife. Here's her reply.
It's addressed to him.
450:
- You'll have lunch with us on New Year's Day?
- We promise!
451:
Such a nice woman. Pity her father's
a fence and a black-marketeer.
452:
What's all the noise? Who said you could go out?
- Look who's here... Bad man.
454:
The New Year has come.
I hope everything changes for you this year.
455:
Anything can happen, but remember:
wherever you are, wherever I am,
456:
I'll always remember you.
I'll be sure to find you.
457:
- And now... One moment...
- Where's he off to?
458:
Who knows? You can't make
head or tail of him anymore.
459:
What's not to understand? He says
he'll find us anywhere and cut our throats.
461:
They say he took a razor to Ryaboy's throat—
snick, goodbye.
- He's turned savage, the jackal.
462:
Who's come to visit you?
Father Frost, with presents for you!
463:
- Fedya, come here. - What have I done?
- Come along. Wear these in good health.
They're for the home.
464:
- What do I need them for? I don't have a home.
- You will. Your life's ahead of you.
465:
- They'll come in handy in prison meanwhile. Wear them.
- Always predicting the worst.
466:
This is for you, Vasya.
Gavrila Petrovich, this is yours.
- Thank you.
467:
- Pure wool.
- This one's for you too.
469: Sour stuff. It's dull without vodka.
470:
- Must you get drunk as a pig?
- What else is there to do?
471: We could sit and have a heart-to-heart.
472:
I'm not a prosecutor. I don't do heart-to-hearts.
- We could play a game.
473:
Look at him! Think I'd play cards with you?
You've got nine aces in your deck.
474: Why does it have to be cards?
475:
Here's a good game: cities.
I say "Moscow,"
476:
so you name one beginning with W:
Warsaw. Then you name one beginning with W:
Wellington. Understand?
477:
Now your turn, Fedya.
A city beginning with N.
478:
Vorkuta.
Why? I did time there.
479:
- All right. Yours begins with A, then.
- Dzhambul. - Where did Dzhambul come from?
480:
It's warm there. My home is there,
and my mother.
481:
Let's play this instead. I'll go out,
you hide something, then I'll come back and find it.
482:
- You'd do better to find our helmet.
- Be quiet.
483:
- We'll hide something while he peeks through a hole?
- No. You can go out and hide.
484:
You make sure I don't peek.
Why me? Whatever it is, it's always Fedya.
485:
- I'll rip your mouth off, you little pest!
- Mouth, mouth...
486:
- Docent, were you ever little?
- Yes.
487:
- Did you have a mother and father?
- Yes.
488:
Why are you so mean?
Why are you like a dog?
490:
- You came on your own.
- Oh, you're here too.
491:
I tried coming to your place,
but I sensed a trap.
492: Mityai, I need somewhere to hide.
494:
- Where are we going?
- Keep moving.
495:
- Sorry to trouble you for nothing, Doctor.
- It's all right.
496:
Give him valerian, some warm tea,
and let him sleep.
- Thank you.
497:
- Does it hurt, Garik?
- It hurts, Vasya. Read it.
499:
"Dear Dad, hello! We found out
you're in prison,
500:
and we were very happy,
because we thought you were dead."
501: What bastard told Khmyr's boy about him?
502:
"Mom was happy too. When your letter came,
she cried all day,
503:
though she used to say
you were a test pilot."
504: More like a thief in flight...
505:
"But I'm still happy you're alive,
because Mom says
506:
you're a good man,
but you have a weak character."
507:
Exactly! Weak character: stole our money
and blamed the taxi driver.
508: Scram! I'll knock your horns off, radish!
510:
Aren't you ashamed? You're forty.
Half your lives are behind you.
511:
What's behind you?
What do you have now? What's ahead?
512:
Darkness, filth, and nothing human!
Come to your senses before it's too late.
That's my advice.
513:
Listen, Docent, we need to clear out.
That doctor will tell the police.
514:
- She won't. - Why not?
- I took a razor to her throat.
515: She's in the well. Go and look.
516: What was my sentence? One year.
517: What will I get for escaping? Three.
518:
For the kindergarten and the apartment?
Say ten.
520:
And I should put up with that snake
for a measly fourteen years?
521:
The one who put the old lady in the well?
Do what you want. I'm going to the police.
522: Go on. He won't touch you.
523:
What about you?
Will you put up with him until you die?
524:
Vasya, I told him the other day
I had a cold, and he...
525:
Enough about your cold.
Come here...
527:
- What are you doing?
- Cleaning the carpet.
528:
Well, comrades, finita la commedia.
First, I'll take this off.
530:
I'll serve my time, and that's it.
I'm going straight! I'll get a job.
531:
- Doing what? Watchman at my old collective farm.
- Why a watchman?
532:
I can clear snow, lay bricks,
or be a translator. I know English.
533:
If only we'd brought back the hat!
What's Docent? A crook.
534:
- Lots of crooks, but only one hat.
- They'd shorten our sentences for the helmet.
535:
Where did he put it?
I thought we'd searched everywhere.
536:
Crook! I told you I had a cold,
and you just said, "I'll rip your mouth off."
537:
- Made me dive in freezing weather!
- When did he make you dive?
538:
When they caught us. Remember?
He said he'd fish, and I had to dive.
539:
- Wait. What did he say about fishing?
- "I'm fishing in an ice hole.
540:
And you, Kosoy, can you swim?"
- He hid the helmet in the ice hole!
541:
Right! I remember, the radish!
It's in the ice hole at Malakhovka!
542:
Why didn't you say so, you lout?
You could've left a note before hanging yourself.
- Let's go.
543:
- What about him?
- Let them collect him. I'm not carrying
a great lump like that. Come on!
545:
- There's nothing there.
- It's on the bottom. You have to dive.
546:
Why me? Whatever it is, it's always Kosoy.
Vasya, tell him to dive himself.
547: I can't! It's cold. I'll get sick.
548:
- He was hanging himself a minute ago,
and now he's afraid of a cold!
- Sporting greetings!
550:
- Where's the boat station?
- Over there.
551:
I'd kill the lot of you
if I had the time!
552:
Now there are two of them.
And another one back at the country house.
554:
- One!
- Well done, Fyodor Petrovich! Well done!
555:
- Two.
- The more we turn in, the better.
